assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational, influential account of reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion that changed behavioural economic analysis and experimental practice.
assessment.attribution: The listed researchers provide a coherent and limited attribution for complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The central findings and their implications have been tested extensively across settings over several decades.
uncertainties: The breadth of social-preference phenomena makes the boundary between this contribution and adjacent behavioural work contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and behavioural game theory supplied durable evidence on strategic behaviour and made laboratory evidence central to economics.
assessment.attribution: Plott, Holt and Camerer are highly identifiable contributors to the experimental-market and behavioural-game-theory strands.
assessment.maturity: The programme is long-established, with a large record of replications, extensions and policy-relevant applications.
uncertainties: The field has several additional major contributors, so any three-person attribution necessarily compresses the intellectual history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Models of present bias, self-control and reference dependence made behavioural departures from standard preferences analytically usable throughout economics.
assessment.attribution: The proposed laureates are central to formalizing dynamic inconsistency and behavioural preference models, while the wider attribution remains difficult.
assessment.maturity: These concepts have generated a mature theoretical and empirical literature with broad use in household, labour and public economics.
uncertainties: Reference dependence and present bias have partly distinct intellectual lineages.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs produced unusually direct evidence on labour-market discrimination and reshaped empirical work on unequal treatment.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are clearly associated with a landmark application; the broader research tradition has many contributors.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been repeatedly deployed, scrutinized and extended across labour markets and countries.
uncertainties: Interpretation of callback differentials and external validity remain active methodological issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods became essential tools for credible empirical analysis where persistence and unobserved heterogeneity complicate identification.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond form a focused attribution for the named methodological advance.
assessment.maturity: The methods are deeply embedded in applied work and their finite-sample and specification limitations are well understood.
uncertainties: Their very widespread use has also exposed risks from weak instruments and invalid moment conditions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The integration of insurance theory with credible measurement greatly advanced understanding of adverse selection and insurance-market design.
assessment.attribution: The three proposed laureates represent closely connected theoretical and empirical elements of the stated contribution.
assessment.maturity: A substantial empirical literature has tested selection mechanisms and informed insurance policy debates.
uncertainties: The magnitude and welfare implications of selection vary substantially across insurance settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed measurement of intergenerational mobility and connected place, policy and opportunity to long-run outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are identifiable leaders of the linked administrative-data research programme.
assessment.maturity: The empirical infrastructure and principal findings have been widely reused, replicated and extended.
uncertainties: Causal interpretations of geographic mobility patterns require stronger assumptions than descriptive measurement alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life conditions and skill formation established the economic importance of health and developmental environments long before adulthood.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond and Cunha make a coherent attribution across empirical early-life evidence and dynamic skill-formation mechanisms.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has accumulated over many cohorts, settings and research designs and has lasting policy relevance.
uncertainties: Separating prenatal or childhood shocks from correlated family and environmental conditions remains empirically demanding.
